presets.name: Search: Google
presets.description: Google web results for {{query}}, pages 1-3 (start=0,10,20). One extract step per page: rows in step order are page 1,2,3; position = row index + 1 within that page. Ads (#tads) are outside #rso and not collected; rows without a result heading (People also ask, carousels) are skipped by the :has(a h3) filter. Inputs: query (required), hl (default en). Captcha: the wait_for #search step fails and the run stops; never solve it. Selectors verified 2026-09-16.

presets.name: Search: Bing
presets.description: Bing web results for a query, pages 1-3 (first=1,11,21). One extract per page (page = step order, position = row index + 1). Only li.b_algo organic rows are read, so ads (li.b_ad) and answer cards are dropped. url is Bing's click-tracking link (bing.com/ck/a, resolves to the page); display_url is the cite text Bing shows. Inputs: query (required). Selectors verified 2026-09-16.

presets.name: Search: DuckDuckGo
presets.description: DuckDuckGo web results for a query, pages 1-3. Page 1 loads with the query, then pages 2 and 3 load by clicking "More results" (#more-results). There's one extract per page, scoped between DDG's own "Page N" separators, so rows never repeat. Rows are li[data-layout=organic] (ads, the Wikipedia box and related searches are dropped). Fields: title, url (the direct link), display_url, snippet. Position = row index + 1 within the page's step. Inputs: query (required). Selectors verified 2026-09-16.

presets.name: Search: Brave
presets.description: Brave Search web results for a query, pages 1-3 (offset=0,1,2). One extract per page. Rows are div.snippet[data-type=web], which leaves out ads, news, video and discussion clusters. Fields: title, url (direct), display_url (cite), snippet (for forum Q&A rows, the inline answer). Brave numbers the rows itself with data-pos, but extract can't read an attribute of the row element, so position = row index + 1. Inputs: query (required). Selectors verified 2026-09-16.

presets.name: Search: Yahoo
presets.description: Yahoo web results for a query, pages 1-3 (b=1,11,21). One extract per page. Rows are #web > ol > li containing .algo, so sponsored blocks, which live in separate lists, are dropped. Fields: title (h3), url (h3 a href, direct), snippet (.compText). Position = row index + 1. Inputs: query (required). Selectors verified 2026-09-16.

presets.name: Google News: topic
presets.description: Google News headlines for a section and edition. Inputs: topic (default TECHNOLOGY), hl (en-US), gl (US), ceid (US:en); for Arabic Egypt use hl=ar, gl=EG, ceid=EG:ar. Fields: headline, label, source, time (ISO), time_text, url, encoded_target. url is Google News's ./read/ redirect (relative to news.google.com). The publisher URL is only present inside the link's jslog attribute, returned as encoded_target: base64 JSON after "5:", whose last string is the article URL. Rows are every story card (jscontroller=BoFkO), including stories nested in full-coverage clusters, capped at limit 40. label is the accessible "headline - source - time - By author" string. Selectors verified 2026-09-16.

inputs.name: topic

presets.name: Google Trends: explore a keyword
presets.description: Google Trends Classic Explore (/trends/explore) for one keyword. The new Gemini Explore page ignores ?q=, so this plugin uses the classic URL. Inputs: keyword (required), geo (empty = worldwide), date (default "today 12-m"). There are three extract steps, and the run's headline result is the last one: (1) interest over time: date and value (0-100) rows, read from the chart's accessible data table; (2) related topics: rank, topic, value, link; (3) related queries: rank, query, value (e.g. Breakout or +250%), link. presets.name: News: read an article
presets.description: Open any article URL and extract it with site-independent selectors only: title (h1), og_title, author (meta author) and author_byline ([rel=author]/[itemprop=author]/author links), published (article:published_time), time (the first time[datetime], inside article when present), modified, canonical, site_name, description, section, lang, json_ld (the first JSON-LD block, which usually holds author and datePublished when the meta tags are missing), body (the plain text of [itemprop=articleBody] or <article>, whichever comes first in the document) and body_main (the plain text of <main>, as a fallback for sites without article markup). A field that doesn't exist on a site comes back null rather than guessed. Input: url (required; its host must be on the browser's allowlist, so any site outside the list is refused). presets.name: Telegram: read a public channel
presets.description: Posts from a public Telegram channel's web preview (t.me/s/<channel>), with no login. Step 3 reads the latest ~20 posts. Then 2 scroll-back passes (3 upward wheel scrolls each, which is what makes the preview lazy-load older posts) are followed by a final extract of every post now on the page, oldest first. That final extract is the run's result. Fields: post_url, date (ISO), text, views, first_link, link_preview, photo, video, document, poll, forwarded_from, author. Media type = whichever of photo/video/document/poll is set. There are no loops, so the number of passes is fixed at 2; for a deeper history make a copy with more scroll steps. Private channels and channels with the preview disabled redirect to t.me/<channel>, and the wait_for step then fails. Input: channel (required). Selectors verified 2026-09-16.

presets.name: Gmail: read a message
presets.description: Opens one Gmail conversation and reads every expanded message in it: subject (conversation), then per message: message_id, legacy_id, from, from_email, to (recipients as shown), date (full, title attribute), date_text, body (plain text of the rendered body, quoted history included as Gmail shows it), body_html. Only the messages Gmail shows expanded come back (usually the latest and any unread); collapsed older messages in long threads are not expanded and are not returned, so a 13-message thread can return 1 row. The subject extract is step 3; the run headline is the message list. Opening an unread conversation marks it as read, exactly as a person opening it would. Inputs: id (required; the legacy_id from gmail-read-inbox, e.g. 1a0a96f93f3e6901), view (default inbox; the folder the id belongs to, e.g. all, sent), account (default 0). Messages are the role=listitem rows holding data-message-id / data-legacy-message-id, h2[data-thread-perm-id] and the email/name attributes; the body uses Gmail's a3s class and the date g3, the least stable hooks. Selectors verified 2026-09-16.

presets.name: Gmail: send an email
presets.description: WRITE plugin: composes and SENDS an email from the signed-in Gmail account. Never run as part of reading. Opens Gmail full-page compose with the recipient prefilled from the URL (?view=cm&fs=1&tf=1&to=…), types the subject, clicks the body and presses ArrowUp 10 times so the caret sits on the empty first line above the signature (Tab lost the text, a plain click put it inside the signature), types the plain-text body, then clicks Send as the final step and waits for "Message sent". Inputs: to (required; address(es), comma separated, no spaces), subject (required), body (required, plain text, single paragraph), account (default 0). Cc/Bcc and attachments are not handled. Hooks: input[name=subjectbox], the Message Body editor reached by Tab, and div[role=button][aria-label^="Send"]. Known: a browser extension build older than the FM-143 fix drops every "." typed (the Mac browser did on 2026-09-16), so update the extension before sending text with periods. Verified up to the final Send click (composer filled and read back, draft discarded, nothing sent). Selectors verified 2026-09-16.

presets.name: YouTube: search videos
presets.description: YouTube search results (youtube.com/results?search_query={{query}}) for the signed-in or signed-out browser: title, url (/watch?v=…, site-relative, with YouTube's pp tracking parameter), channel, channel_url (/@handle), views (e.g. 2.3M views), age (e.g. 4 years ago), duration (e.g. 1:07:53; empty for live streams), description (the result snippet), label (accessible title + spoken duration), thumbnail (null for rows below the fold whose image has not lazy-loaded). Only video results are collected (ytd-video-renderer): shorts shelves, channels, playlists and ads are skipped. The page is scrolled down three times before reading, so YouTube's infinite list has loaded more rows (typically 20-40); the single extract at the end reads every row loaded, capped by limit. Inputs: query (required; spaces are fine), filter (optional sp= code from YouTube's filter URL, e.g. EgIQAQ%3D%3D = videos only, CAI%3D = upload date), limit (default 40). Hooks: YouTube's custom element names (ytd-video-renderer, ytd-channel-name, #metadata-line, #video-title), not generated classes. Selectors verified 2026-09-16.

presets.name: YouTube: read a video
presets.description: Reads one YouTube watch page (youtube.com/watch?v={{id}}). Step 3 extract (video): title, channel, channel_url, subscribers, views_and_date (the info line, e.g. "2.3M views 4 years ago"), date (the info tooltip: exact view count and upload date, e.g. "2,305,815 views • Oct 7, 2021 • #tags"), likes (like button's accessible label), description (the inline description as rendered, which is truncated with "...more" unless expanded), comment_count (e.g. "1,234 Comments"). Then it scrolls 4 times so comments load, and step 9 extract (the run's headline result) returns the top comments: author, author_url, text, published, likes (vote count), replies (the "N replies" button text), pinned. Only the comments loaded by those scrolls come back (typically 20), in YouTube's default "Top comments" order; replies are not expanded. Inputs: id (required; the v= value, e.g. 446E-r0rXHI), limit (default 40). When comments are turned off, the comment wait fails and the run stops with that reason. Hooks: YouTube's custom element names (ytd-watch-metadata, ytd-comment-thread-renderer, #content-text, #vote-count-middle), not generated classes. Only the last extract is quoted in the run result; the video extract is kept as that step's artifact. Selectors verified 2026-09-16.

presets.name: YouTube: comment on a video
presets.description: WRITE plugin: POSTS a top-level comment on a YouTube video as the signed-in channel. Never run as part of reading. Opens youtube.com/watch?v={{id}}, scrolls to the comments, clicks the "Add a comment…" box (#simplebox-placeholder), types the text into the editor (#contenteditable-root), then clicks the Comment button (#submit-button) as the final step. Inputs: id (required; the v= value), text (required; plain text). Replies to other comments are not handled. Fails at the comment box when comments are off or the browser is signed out. Hooks: YouTube's element ids in ytd-comment-simplebox-renderer. Verified up to the final Comment click (filled editor read back and screenshotted, then Cancel; nothing posted). Fields: author, handle, text, time (ISO), url (/handle/status/id), counts (the action bar aria-label, e.g. "12 replies, 5 reposts, 40 likes, 3 bookmarks, 1000 views"), replies, reposts, likes, social_context (e.g. "X reposted" / "Pinned"). Passes are fixed at 3 because there are no loops. Input: timeline (default https://x.com/home). Selectors are X's data-testid attributes, verified 2026-09-16.

presets.name: Facebook: read the news feed
presets.description: Facebook home feed (facebook.com) for the signed-in account, collected in 3 passes: extract, scroll ~2 screens, extract, scroll, extract. presets.name: WhatsApp: send a message to a number (verified)
presets.description: WRITE (FM-275): sends one text message to the WhatsApp number in {{phone}} from the WhatsApp Web session in the browser . It opens web.whatsapp.com/send?phone=… and waits for the chat composer. If WhatsApp reports an invalid number, the composer never appears and the run stops before typing. It then runs a read-only check that throws, which stops the run before anything is typed, unless the chat header shows a phone number equal to {{phone}} digit for digit. Clicking the header to open Contact info detached the browser debugger (runs 2ba58ef2, 8ac2385b), so the panel isn't opened. As a result, a number saved as a named contact (header shows a name) is REFUSED rather than guessed; unsave it or extend the check once the panel can be read. Only then does it type, record the chat title and composer, press Enter (sends) and read the chat back. The server should only call it for allow-listed numbers. Inputs: phone, text (required). Selectors (data-testid) verified 2026-09-17.

Run it only after a person has confirmed the exact share, one share at a time, after a person confirmed that exact share, and only into groups marked for promotion. Opens the group, clicks "Start a public post", types message then link into the "Create post modal" editor ([role=dialog] [contenteditable=true]), waits for the enabled Post button (button.share-actions__primary-action) and clicks it as the final step. Inputs: group_url, message, link. Verified up to (not including) the Post click by the twin linkedin-group-share-dryrun, run abb68261 on 2026-09-17: the editor read back the exact 85 characters, punctuation and URL included.

presets.name: X: my latest posts
presets.description: READ (FM-347): the signed-in account's newest posts, for finding the URL of a post x-post just published (x-post does not return it). Opens x.com/home, follows the Profile link (so it works for whichever account is signed in), and extracts the first 8 posts: url (/<handle>/status/<id>, the link around the post's time), text (tweetText) and time (ISO). A pinned post can be first; the social module matches by text. Nothing is clicked except the Profile link. Verified 2026-09-17.

presets.name: Threads: my latest posts
presets.description: READ (FM-347): the signed-in account's newest Threads posts, for finding the URL of a post threads-post just published (threads-post does not return it). Opens threads.com, follows the Profile link (the first /@handle link, for whichever account is signed in), and extracts the first 8 post rows: url (/@handle/post/<code>, the link around the time), time (ISO) and text (the row's text, which starts with the handle and the relative time before the post body). Nothing is clicked except the Profile link. Verified 2026-09-17.
